rationale:
ROUND 2 on the same correlation. Round 1 was REVISE, gated by editquality, and BOTH objections were right — both about this submission rather than the code.

(a) HIGH: I listed 'a sibling test refuses a stale exemption' as one of three anti-vacuity controls but named only ONE test symbol in the edits, so the plan promised a mechanism it did not show. The mechanism EXISTS in the committed file (TestLockBlindPlanReadersAreAllStillPlanSectionReaders); the omission was in the plan. It is now edit 3, with its body. This is the same failure the 285 round-1 gate caught — asserting a symbol's behaviour without putting the symbol in front of the reviewer.

(b) MEDIUM, and this one was a FALSE FIGURE, not a presentation gap: I wrote '6 readers, 2 merge, 4 declared' while the map listed FIVE declared files. The true population, re-derived by running the detector rather than re-reading my note, is SEVEN readers: 2 merge, 5 declared. The stale 6/2/4 was the count taken BEFORE this test's own first run found check_sectionless_pages. I recorded the discovery in three places and never re-derived the total — so a figure the whole design's scope argument rests on was wrong in the register entry, the RFC, the test's header comment and this submission. Corrected in all four, each carrying a visible note of what it used to say. WRONG_CALLS row written: a census that gains a member has a NEW TOTAL, and the total is the part everything else quotes.

Unchanged from round 1 and still the substance: RFC_033 was opened at this council's architecture seat's direction on the bugs_closed/285 fix (corr 79f70435, APPROVED with needs_rfc) and ruled by the owner on 2026-08-17 — build the source-scan lockstep, NOT a single mandatory entrypoint. One test file. It scans actions/, actions/*/ and datahelpers/ for files that read site_plan_sections (FROM or JOIN, comments stripped) and requires each either to call the merge or to be declared in lockBlindPlanReaders WITH A REASON.

WHY site_plan_sections AND NOT pages.sections. The plan is the store that structurally cannot know about a lock; the cache now carries the merged list (live, proven on natural rebuilds of loancalculator.co.uk/index 08-16 and webdesign.uk/contact 08-17), so a cache reader gets locked rows for free. Scoping to the cache too would fire on ~18 files and teach authors to add a line to a list rather than think.

WHY NOT ONE ENTRYPOINT. The readers legitimately want different answers and one must NOT merge: page_section_satisfiability PREDICTS the loader and must mirror its refusal when no tier serves; ensure_page_section_layout acts only when every source is empty, the same case the loader declines; reconcile_site_plan compares plan version to plan version, where a live row belongs to neither; plan_section_counts is a dedup ALLOWANCE whose victims already exclude locked rows.

HONEST LIMITS. It reads SOURCE: it proves the call exists, not that it executes on the path that matters. It cannot see a reader in a package outside its three globbed roots, and cannot tell that case from 'no such reader exists'.

plan.summary: RFC_033 option 2, owner-ruled: a source-scan lockstep so a NEW reader of site_plan_sections must decide, in writing, whether it honours human locks. Round 2 corrects the submission: the stale-exemption test is now shown as its own edit, and the population figure is corrected from 6/2/4 to the measured 7 readers (2 merge, 5 declared).

edits.rationale: Scans three roots for FROM|JOIN site_plan_sections after stripping line comments; a reader must call the merge or be declared with a reason. TWO anti-vacuity controls live in THIS symbol — (1) it fails if it sees NO readers at all (a detector that silently stopped matching would otherwise pass by finding nothing), and (2) it pins the two known merge-callers BY NAME, so deleting the merge from the loader fails here instead of quietly leaving zero offenders. The third control is a separate test, edit 3.

The exemption map IS the deliverable, so each entry states the mechanism, not a shrug. FIVE entries, matching the measured population of 7 readers (2 merge, 5 declared): ensure_page_section_layout (acts only when EVERY source is empty, the same case the loader declines; merging would suppress the scaffold and strand the page); page_section_satisfiability (predicts the loader, so it must mirror the loader's refusal, else it promises a build that no-ops — the false promise bugs_closed/177 was filed for); reconcile_site_plan (plan-version-to-plan-version restamp comparison, and its own header says deliberately not against pages.sections; a live locked row is in neither version and would make every locked page read as re-composed for ever); plan_section_counts (a dedup ALLOWANCE denominator whose victim pool already excludes locked rows via the agent-writable predicate, so merging would raise the allowance without adding a candidate and a real duplicate would survive — pin-predicate-is-not-the-pool-predicate applied to a count); check_sectionless_pages (reads the plan for the SIBLING's layout, not the subject's membership).
edits.sketch: "page_section_satisfiability.go": "predicts the loader, so it must mirror the loader's refusal to merge when no tier serves; counting locked rows would promise a build that no-ops",

edits.rationale: The third anti-vacuity control, named in round 1's rationale but not shown as an edit — which is what the gating objection was, and it was right. It refuses a STALE exemption: every entry in lockBlindPlanReaders must still be readable, must still match readsThePlansSections, and must still carry a non-empty reason. Without it the map becomes a car park — a file parked there years ago would silently cover a future lock-blind read that lands in it, which is the same 'declared once, true never again' failure the register's stale-status landmine describes.

plan.risks: (1) SOURCE-SCAN, NOT BEHAVIOUR: it proves a call exists, not that it runs on the path that matters. Stated in the file header rather than left for a reviewer to find. (2) The exemption map is a second hand-written census and will rot if nobody re-reads the reasons; the sibling test only checks that each entry is still a reader, not that its reason is still true. (3) Scope choice: cache readers are deliberately NOT covered, which is only safe while the loader keeps writing the merged list to pages.sections -- if that write is ever removed, this test's scoping argument silently becomes wrong, and nothing here would notice. That dependency is named in the header. (4) The three glob roots are a judgement about where readers live; a reader in a package outside them is invisible, and the test cannot tell that case from 'no such reader exists'. (5) ROUND-1 LESSON, recorded rather than smoothed over: the population figure this design's scope argument rests on was WRONG in the submission, the register entry, the RFC and the test's own header, because a correction that ADDED a member was recorded in three places without re-deriving the total. The count is now produced by running the detector, and the test header says what it used to say. A reviewer should treat any other census figure I have written on this lane as needing the same re-derivation.
